title: Soft Skill Assessment - Set 21
description: Evaluates commercial mathematics, deductive arrangements, contextual business English, and architectural sprint communication.

questions.question_text: A dishonest dealer sells goods at a 10% loss on cost price but uses a weight that is 20% less than the true weight. What is his actual profit or loss percentage?
questions.explanation: Let true cost of 1000g be ₹1000. Selling price for 1000g nominal = 1000 × 0.90 = ₹900. But he delivers only 800g (20% less). Cost of 800g to dealer = ₹800. Profit = 900 - 800 = ₹100. Profit % = (100 / 800) × 100 = 12.5% profit.

questions.question_text: If 25% of a number is subtracted from the number itself, the result is 150. What is the number?
A train passes two men walking in the direction opposite to that of the train at speeds of 5 m/s and 10 m/s in 6 seconds and 5 seconds respectively. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: Let train speed be v (m/s) and length be L. L = (v + 5) × 6 and L = (v + 10) × 5. 6v + 30 = 5v + 50 => v = 20 m/s. Length L = (20 + 5) × 6 = 25 × 6 = 150 m.

questions.question_text: Pipe A can fill an oil cistern in 15 minutes, Pipe B in 20 minutes, and Pipe C can empty it in 30 minutes. If all three pipes are kept open simultaneously in an empty cistern, in how many minutes will it be full?
questions.explanation: Net rate per minute = 1/15 + 1/20 - 1/30 = (4 + 3 - 2)/60 = 5/60 = 1/12. It takes 12 minutes to fill the cistern.

questions.question_text: Find the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on ₹15,000 for 2 years at 8% per annum.
The average of 8 consecutive even numbers is 43. What is the sum of the smallest and largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: In an arithmetic progression, the sum of the first and last term is equal to twice the average: 2 × 43 = 86 (the numbers are 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50; 36 + 50 = 86).

questions.question_text: A can do a piece of work in 10 days and B in 15 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: Total work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units. A's rate = 3 units/day, B's rate = 2 units/day. In a 2-day cycle, work done = 3 + 2 = 5 units. To complete 30 units: (30 / 5) = 6 cycles = 6 × 2 = 12 days.

questions.question_text: What is the units digit of the product (784 × 618 × 917 × 463)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the units digits: 4 × 8 = 32 (units digit 2). 2 × 7 = 14 (units digit 4). 4 × 3 = 12 (units digit 2). The units digit is 2.

questions.question_text: Find the missing number in the sequence: 7, 26, 63, 124, 215, ?
In a certain code, 'CLOUD' is written as 'ENQWF'. How is 'RAINY' written in that same pattern?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 2: R(18)+2=T, A(1)+2=C, I(9)+2=K, N(14)+2=P, Y(25)+2=A, yielding TCKPA.

questions.question_text: Pointing to a man, a girl said, 'He is the only son of the father of my brother-in-law's wife.' If the brother-in-law has only one brother, how is the man related to the girl's sister?
questions.explanation: My brother-in-law's wife is my sister. The father of my sister is my father. The only son of my father is my brother (and my sister's brother).

questions.question_text: Statements: No printer is a scanner. All scanners are photocopiers. Some photocopiers are fax machines. Conclusions: I. Some photocopiers are not printers. II. Some fax machines are scanners.
questions.explanation: Since all scanners are photocopiers and no scanner is a printer, those photocopiers which are scanners cannot be printers (I follows). Fax machines only have a partial overlap with photocopiers, not necessarily scanners (II does not follow).

questions.question_text: SCULPTURE : CHISEL :: PAINTING : ?
questions.explanation: A chisel is the primary creating tool used to carve a sculpture; a brush is the primary creating tool used to create a painting.

questions.question_text: A drone flies 8 km South, turns West and flies 6 km, then turns North and flies 8 km. How far is the drone from its takeoff pad?
questions.explanation: South 8 km and North 8 km cancel out. The drone is exactly 6 km West of the takeoff pad.

questions.question_text: Find the odd one out among the numbers: 28, 42, 56, 70, 85
questions.explanation: 28, 42, 56, and 70 are all divisible by 14; 85 is not.

questions.question_text: Choose the synonym of 'ANACHRONISTIC':

questions.question_text: Choose the antonym of 'FASTIDIOUS':

questions.question_text: Select the sentence that correctly employs the subjunctive mood after a verb of recommendation:
options: The architect recommended that the database cluster is reconfigured.
The architect recommended that the database cluster be reconfigured.
The architect recommended that the database cluster was reconfigured.
The architect recommended that the database cluster should be reconfigured.
questions.explanation: Mandative subjunctive constructions use the base form of the verb ('that the cluster be reconfigured').

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The compliance officer was oblivious ___ the architectural security violations in the subsystem.
questions.explanation: 'Oblivious to' is the standard modern English idiom (or 'oblivious of', but 'oblivious to' is the primary modern standard).

questions.question_text: What does the idiom 'to burn the candle at both ends' mean?
options: To work excessively hard from early morning until late at night
To ignite a dual fire hazard
To divide an engineering task equally
questions.explanation: 'To burn the candle at both ends' means to exhaust oneself by doing too much, especially going to bed late and getting up early.

questions.question_text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'A person who acts as a diplomat and promotes goodwill between organizations'
questions.explanation: An 'Ambassador' is an official envoy, diplomat, or promoter of goodwill and institutional collaboration.

questions.question_text: During a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack on your core API, the infrastructure auto-scaler costs begin spiking by $5,000 per hour. What should the incident lead do?
options: Turn off all servers and let customers see an offline error.

Activate Web Application Firewall (WAF) rate limiting and edge DDoS mitigation rules, analyze malicious IP patterns, and filter traffic at the CDN level rather than absorbing bad traffic with expensive compute.
Ignore the cost and hope the attacker gets tired.
questions.explanation: Mitigating volumetric attacks at the edge (CDN/WAF) drops malicious traffic before it hits compute, preventing cloud billing runaway.

questions.question_text: A client notices that your team's software is logging IP addresses and asks whether this violates GDPR compliance. How should the engineering lead respond?
options: Deny that IP addresses are ever collected.
Explain the technical necessity (security audit trails, rate limiting), verify data retention windows and encryption, and provide the client with the official Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
Immediately delete all system logs across all servers.
Tell the client that privacy laws don't apply to your product.
questions.explanation: Transparent legal compliance (DPA) and articulating legitimate security auditing interests builds enterprise client trust.

questions.question_text: You are pair-programming with a teammate who is struggling with a recursion concept. How can you best assist them?
options: Grab the keyboard and write the entire solution yourself without explaining.
Encourage them to draw out the call stack with a simple base case, ask guiding questions, and let them type the solution while you navigate.
Tell them recursion is too advanced for them.
questions.explanation: Driver-navigator pair programming where the learner types and reasons through the call stack fosters deep conceptual mastery.

questions.question_text: Your company has a policy requiring two peer approvals before merging to production. An executive demands an immediate hotfix push without any review. What should you do?
options: Push the code immediately without review to please the executive.
Expedite a 5-minute emergency peer review with an on-call senior engineer to satisfy the safety guardrail while maintaining rapid deployment speed.
Refuse to talk to the executive and shut down your computer.
questions.explanation: Expediting emergency peer reviews upholds mandatory compliance and safety guardrails without causing unnecessary operational gridlock.

title: Soft Skill Assessment - Set 22
description: Tests alligation ratios, blood relationship networks, structural business English, and high-stakes cross-team coordination.

questions.question_text: In what ratio must a merchant mix two varieties of tea costing ₹180 per kg and ₹240 per kg, so that by selling the mixture at ₹231 per kg, he gains 10%?
questions.explanation: Selling price of mixture = ₹231 at 10% gain => Mean cost price = 231 / 1.10 = ₹210 per kg. Using alligation: (240 - 210) : (210 - 180) = 30 : 30 = 1:1.

questions.question_text: A student scored 28% marks and failed by 14 marks. Another student scored 36% marks and obtained 18 marks more than the minimum passing marks. What was the maximum marks in the exam?
questions.explanation: Difference in percentage = 36% - 28% = 8%. Difference in marks = 18 - (-14) = 32 marks. Total maximum marks = (32 / 8) × 100 = 400.

questions.question_text: A motorboat whose speed in still water is 15 km/h goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Total time = 30/(15 + s) + 30/(15 - s) = 4.5. Testing s = 5: Downstream = 30/20 = 1.5 hr. Upstream = 30/10 = 3 hr. Total = 1.5 + 3 = 4.5 hr. Thus, stream speed = 5 km/h.

questions.question_text: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a cistern in 6 hours. After working together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B fill the remaining part in 7 hours. The number of hours taken by C alone to fill the cistern is:
questions.explanation: Work done in 2 hours = 2/6 = 1/3. Remaining work = 2/3. (A + B) do 2/3 work in 7 hours => (A + B) full time = 7 × (3/2) = 10.5 hr = 21/2 hr. Rate of C = 1/6 - 2/21 = (7 - 4)/42 = 3/42 = 1/14. C takes 14 hours alone.

questions.question_text: A committee of 5 members is to be formed from 5 men and 5 women. In how many ways can the committee be chosen if it must have a majority of women?
questions.explanation: Majority of women in 5 members means either (3 women, 2 men), (4 women, 1 man), or (5 women, 0 men). Ways = (5C3 × 5C2) + (5C4 × 5C1) + (5C5 × 5C0) = (10 × 10) + (5 × 5) + (1 × 1) = 100 + 25 + 1 = 126.

questions.question_text: The simple interest on a sum of money is 4/9 of the principal and the number of years is equal to the annual rate percent. What is the rate percent?
The average monthly salary of 20 employees in an office is ₹35,000. If the manager's salary is included, the average increases by ₹2,000. What is the manager's monthly salary?
questions.explanation: Manager's salary = New average + (Original count × increase) = 37,000 + (20 × 2,000) = 37,000 + 40,000 = ₹77,000.

questions.question_text: What is the HCF of 144, 216, and 324?
Complete the series: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, ?

questions.explanation: Direct alphabetical positions: O=15, C=3, E=5, A=1, N=14, giving 15-3-5-1-14.

questions.question_text: A's mother is sister of B and has a daughter C. How can A be related to B if A is male?
questions.explanation: A is the son of B's sister. The son of one's sister is a nephew.

questions.question_text: Statements: All routers are gateways. Some gateways are bridges. No bridge is a switch. Conclusions: I. Some gateways are routers. II. Some gateways are not switches.
questions.explanation: Since all routers are gateways, some gateways are routers (I follows). Since some gateways are bridges and no bridge is a switch, those bridge-gateways cannot be switches (II follows). Both follow.

questions.question_text: COIN : MINT :: WINE : ?
questions.explanation: A coin is manufactured in a mint; wine is produced in a winery or vineyard/winery (Vineyard/Winery).

questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(12² + 9²) = √(144 + 81) = √225 = 15 km.

questions.question_text: Choose the antonym of 'TACIT':

questions.question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly applies the correlative pair 'not only... but also' with parallel predicates:

The patch not only fixed the latency issue but also it reduced memory usage.
The patch fixed not only the latency issue but also reducing memory usage.
Not only the patch fixed the latency issue but also reduced memory usage.
questions.explanation: Both elements after 'not only' and 'but also' must be grammatically parallel past tense verbs ('fixed... reduced').

questions.explanation: 'Privy to' is the standard English idiom meaning sharing in the knowledge of something secret.

questions.question_text: What does the idiom 'to jump the gun' mean?
options: To engage in track and field athletics
To act prematurely before the proper or permitted time
questions.explanation: 'To jump the gun' means to act or start doing something too early, before the proper time.

questions.question_text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'A person who is known for exceptional knowledge and discerning taste in culinary arts or fine wine'
questions.explanation: A 'Connoisseur' is an expert judge in matters of taste and fine arts.

questions.question_text: Your automated CI/CD pipeline triggers an alert indicating that a new database index migration will cause a table lock for 30 minutes on a 50M-row production table. What is the correct engineering response?
options: Execute the migration during peak traffic anyway.
Cancel the immediate deploy, research non-blocking concurrent index creation syntax (e.g., CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in PostgreSQL), test it in staging, and re-schedule.
Delete half the database rows to make the migration faster.
questions.explanation: High-availability databases require online, non-blocking concurrent DDL statements to prevent prolonged production table locks.

questions.question_text: An executive sponsor asks your engineering team to skip writing automated end-to-end regression tests for a new checkout feature to meet an end-of-quarter deadline. How should you respond?
options: Refuse rudely and file a grievance with HR.
Explain that skipping automated regression tests creates compounding technical debt and high risk of revenue loss, and propose launching a scoped MVP with complete test coverage instead.
Delete all existing tests to prove you are fast.
Agree to write tests after production releases, knowing they will never get done.
questions.explanation: Negotiating scope reduction while maintaining automated test integrity protects customer reliability and prevents production regressions.

questions.question_text: You notice that an internal Slack channel contains repeated jokes making light of mental health and neurodiversity. What should you do?
options: Join in the joking to fit in with the group.
Speak up respectfully in the channel or report the behavior to people operations to uphold an inclusive, safe workplace culture.
Forward the jokes to external social media.
questions.explanation: Upholding an inclusive workplace requires active allyship and setting clear professional boundaries against exclusionary humor.

questions.question_text: During an interview debrief, a colleague votes against hiring a candidate solely based on the candidate's university background, despite outstanding problem-solving and system design scores. How do you respond?
options: Agree that only graduates from top colleges should be hired.
Advocate for meritocracy, point to the candidate's concrete rubric scores on algorithms and system design, and redirect the evaluation to documented job competencies.
Accuse your colleague of malice and shout.
Ignore the debrief and leave the room.
questions.explanation: Objective competency-based hiring anchors decisions to demonstrated skills on the evaluation rubric rather than pedigree bias.

title: Soft Skill Assessment - Set 23
description: Evaluates speed-distance mechanics, deductive syllogisms, advanced syntax, and crisis incident management.

questions.question_text: Two trains start at the same time from stations A and B, 200 km apart, and travel towards each other. They meet after 2 hours. If one train travels 10 km/h faster than the other, what is the speed of the faster train?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = Distance / Time = 200 / 2 = 100 km/h. Let speeds be v and (v + 10). v + v + 10 = 100 => 2v = 90 => v = 45 km/h. Faster train speed = 45 + 10 = 55 km/h.

questions.question_text: If 8 men can complete a project in 15 days working 6 hours a day, in how many days can 10 men finish the same project working 8 hours a day?
A sum of ₹8,000 invested at compound interest grows to ₹9,261 in 3 years. What is the rate of interest per annum, compounded annually?

Two pipes can fill a cistern in 12 minutes and 15 minutes respectively. An outlet pipe can drain 30 litres per minute. If all three pipes working together fill the empty cistern in 20 minutes, what is the capacity of the cistern?
questions.explanation: Drain pipe rate = 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 = (5 + 4 - 3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 cistern/min. The drain pipe takes 10 minutes to empty the full cistern. Capacity = 10 minutes × 30 L/min = 300 litres.

questions.question_text: What is the probability that a leap year selected at random will contain 53 Sundays?
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 extra days. The 2 extra days can be (Sun,Mon), (Mon,Tue), (Tue,Wed), (Wed,Thu), (Thu,Fri), (Fri,Sat), or (Sat,Sun) [7 possibilities]. Sunday appears in 2 of these pairs: (Sat,Sun) and (Sun,Mon). Probability = 2/7.

questions.question_text: The marked price of a tablet is ₹18,000. If the dealer offers a discount of 15%, what is the selling price?

If 'EARTH' is coded as 'HDVUK', how is 'VENUS' coded in that same pattern?

questions.question_text: Pointing to an old man, Kailash said, 'His son is my son's uncle.' How is the old man related to Kailash?
questions.explanation: Kailash's son's uncle is Kailash's brother. If the old man's son is Kailash's brother, the old man is Kailash's father.

questions.question_text: Statements: All laptops are screens. All screens are displays. Some displays are monitors. Conclusions: I. All laptops are displays. II. Some monitors are laptops.
questions.explanation: Laptops are inside screens, which are inside displays, so all laptops are displays (I follows). Monitors only intersect displays, not necessarily laptops (II does not follow).

questions.question_text: COURT : JUSTICE :: SCHOOL : ?
questions.explanation: A court is an institution dedicated to administering justice; a school is an institution dedicated to providing education.

Find the odd one out: 19, 23, 29, 37, 45

Although the automated test suite passed, the deployment was delayed due to latency spikes.

questions.explanation: 'Part with' is the correct prepositional collocation when referring to giving up possession of an item.

questions.question_text: What does the idiom 'to leave someone in the lurch' mean?

To give someone an unexpected surprise gift
To guide someone through an unfamiliar maze
To introduce someone to new colleagues
questions.explanation: 'To leave someone in the lurch' means to abandon or desert someone in a difficult or awkward predicament.

questions.question_text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'One who walks in their sleep'
questions.explanation: A 'Somnambulist' is a person who sleepwalks.

questions.question_text: A developer on your squad repeatedly pushes code directly to the main branch bypassing pull request CI/CD gates. How should the engineering lead address this?
options: Revoke their entire GitHub access without saying anything.
Configure branch protection rules to programmatically enforce PR reviews, and have a private mentoring session explaining how branch gates protect production stability.
Shout at them in the all-hands meeting.
questions.explanation: Automating branch protection eliminates human error while private mentoring reinforces the systemic rationale for code review.

questions.question_text: Your team's software depends on a third-party SMS vendor that begins dropping 40% of verification codes during peak hours. What should the engineering lead do?
options: Tell users that SMS verification is impossible.
Implement an automated multi-vendor fallback routing mechanism so failed SMS messages seamlessly retry across a secondary provider like Twilio or AWS SNS.
Turn off two-factor authentication for all accounts.
Wait two weeks for the vendor to fix their servers.
questions.explanation: Enterprise resilience mandates multi-provider redundancy for critical customer verification funnels.

questions.question_text: You are assigned to onboard a new software engineer who has never worked with your cloud platform before. What is the most effective approach?
options: Tell them to read the entire AWS documentation library.
Set up their developer environment together, walk through a 'Good First Issue' pull request, and schedule daily 15-minute syncs during their first sprint.
Assign them a complex distributed systems bug on day one.
Leave them alone until they ask for help.
questions.explanation: Guided walkthroughs of starter tasks and dedicated daily touchpoints accelerate developer onboarding and confidence.

questions.question_text: A critical customer discovers that an API endpoint returns slightly stale data due to a Redis cache invalidation lag. How do you communicate this?
options: Acknowledge the eventual consistency trade-off transparently, provide documentation on the cache TTL window, and offer an option to bypass cache via an explicit query parameter if real-time consistency is mandatory.
Delete the Redis cache and slow down the entire platform.
Blame the customer for querying too frequently.
questions.explanation: Explaining architectural eventual consistency while providing a synchronous cache-bypass option empowers enterprise customers.

title: Soft Skill Assessment - Set 24
description: Tests proportional work kinetics, logical seating arrangements, verbal precision, and executive risk governance.

questions.question_text: A work can be completed by 12 men in 18 days. Six days after they started working, 4 more men joined them. How many days will all of them take to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Remaining work for 12 men = 18 - 6 = 12 days of work. Total man-days remaining = 12 × 12 = 144 man-days. New number of men = 12 + 4 = 16 men. Time = 144 / 16 = 9 days.

questions.question_text: The ratio of milk and water in 55 litres of mixture is 7:4. How much water must be added to make the ratio 7:6?
questions.explanation: Milk = (7/11) × 55 = 35 litres. Water = (4/11) × 55 = 20 litres. To have Milk:Water = 7:6 with 35 litres of milk: Water needed = (6/7) × 35 = 30 litres. Additional water = 30 - 20 = 10 litres.

questions.question_text: A train 180 m long moving at 72 km/h overtakes another train 120 m long moving in the same direction at 54 km/h. In how many seconds does the faster train completely pass the slower one?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m. Relative speed = 72 - 54 = 18 km/h = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s. Time = 300 / 5 = 60 seconds.

questions.question_text: A sum of ₹10,000 is divided into two parts such that simple interest on the first part for 4 years at 8% per annum is equal to simple interest on the second part for 2 years at 10% per annum. What is the first part?
In how many ways can 7 different books be distributed among 3 students such that each student gets at least one book?
questions.explanation: Using Stirling numbers of second kind or inclusion-exclusion: 3^7 - 3C1 × 2^7 + 3C2 × 1^7 = 2187 - 3(128) + 3(1) = 2187 - 384 + 3 = 1,806 ways.

questions.question_text: The average age of 30 students in a class is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average increases by 1 year. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation: Teacher's age = New average + (Original count × increase) = 15 + (30 × 1) = 15 + 30 = 45 years.

questions.question_text: A man covers half his journey at 30 km/h and the remaining half at 60 km/h. If his total travel time was 9 hours, what was the total distance of the journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal halves = (2 × 30 × 60) / (30 + 60) = 3600 / 90 = 40 km/h. Total distance = Average speed × Time = 40 × 9 = 360 km.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper buys an article for ₹500 and sells it for ₹625. What is his profit percentage?
Find the missing number in the sequence: 5, 10, 26, 50, 122, ?
questions.explanation: Squares of consecutive prime numbers + 1: 2²+1=5, 3²+1=10, 5²+1=26, 7²+1=50, 11²+1=122, 13²+1 = 169 + 1 = 170.

questions.question_text: In a certain code, 'ZEBRA' is written as '26-5-2-18-1'. How is 'TIGER' written?
questions.explanation: Direct alphabetical positions: T=20, I=9, G=7, E=5, R=18, giving 20-9-7-5-18.

questions.question_text: Introducing a woman, a man said, 'Her mother's husband's sister is my aunt.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: Her mother's husband is her father. Her father's sister is her aunt. If her aunt is also my aunt, she and I are siblings (or cousins). Here 'Sister' is the primary relation.

questions.question_text: Statements: All cars are engines. No engine is an electric motor. All electric motors are batteries. Conclusions: I. No car is an electric motor. II. Some batteries are electric motors.
questions.explanation: Cars are inside engines, and no engine is an electric motor, so no car is an electric motor (I follows). Since all electric motors are batteries, some batteries are electric motors (II follows). Both follow.

questions.question_text: LIBRARY : BOOKS :: VAULT : ?
questions.explanation: A library is a secure repository for books; a vault is a secure repository for valuables/money.

questions.question_text: Choose the antonym of 'VENERATE':

questions.question_text: Your team is integrating with an external vendor API whose SLA guarantees 99.9% uptime, but during the trial period it drops to 96%. What should you advise product leadership?
options: Proceed to production and hope the vendor improves.

questions.question_text: A cistern has two pipes A and B. Pipe A can fill it in 4 hours and pipe B can empty it in 6 hours. If both pipes are opened together when the cistern is empty, in how many hours will the cistern be full?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/4 - 1/6 = (3 - 2)/12 = 1/12 cistern/hour. The cistern fills in 12 hours.

questions.question_text: If 40% of a number is 240, what is 60% of that number?
A car completes a journey of 400 km in 8 hours. If it covers the first half of the distance at 40 km/h, at what speed must it cover the remaining half to finish on time?
questions.explanation: First half = 200 km at 40 km/h => time = 200 / 40 = 5 hours. Total time = 8 hours => Remaining time = 8 - 5 = 3 hours. Required speed for second 200 km = 200 / 3 = 66.67 km/h.

questions.question_text: The simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 7% per annum is ₹1,050. What is the principal?
A bag contains 4 red, 5 green, and 6 white balls. A ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is not green?
questions.explanation: Total balls = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15. Balls that are not green = 4 red + 6 white = 10. Probability = 10 / 15 = 2/3.

questions.question_text: By selling a watch for ₹1,140, a shopkeeper loses 5%. What was the cost price of the watch?

questions.question_text: Pointing to a man, a woman said, 'His father's only sister is my aunt.' How is the woman related to that man?
questions.explanation: His father's sister is his aunt. If she is also the woman's aunt, the man and the woman are siblings (or cousins). Here 'Sister' is the primary family relation.

questions.question_text: Statements: All monitors are screens. No screen is a printer. All printers are hardware. Conclusions: I. No monitor is a printer. II. Some hardware are printers.
questions.explanation: Monitors are inside screens, and no screen is a printer, so no monitor is a printer (I follows). Since all printers are hardware, some hardware are printers (II follows). Both follow.

questions.question_text: DOCTOR : STETHOSCOPE :: ASTRONOMER : ?
questions.explanation: A doctor uses a stethoscope to observe patients; an astronomer uses a telescope to observe celestial objects.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the correlative pair 'neither... nor':
options: Neither the frontend client nor the backend API was able to reproduce the bug.
Neither the frontend client or the backend API was able to reproduce the bug.
Neither the frontend client nor the backend API were not able to reproduce the bug.
Neither the frontend client nor the backend API were able to reproduce the bug.
questions.explanation: When two singular subjects ('client', 'API') are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb is singular ('was able').

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The engineering lead was skeptical ___ the vendor's claims of zero latency.

questions.question_text: What does the idiom 'to steal someone's thunder' mean?
options: To take credit for someone else's ideas or accomplishments
questions.explanation: 'To steal someone's thunder' means to take praise or attention away from someone by anticipating their ideas or doing something first.

questions.question_text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'A person who is indifferent or hostile to culture, the arts, or intellectual pursuits'
questions.explanation: A 'Philistine' is a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts.

questions.question_text: A critical payment reconciliation service fails to balance accounts at midnight due to a floating-point rounding issue. What should the engineering lead mandate?
options: Round all customer balances up by $1 to hide the discrepancy.
Switch all financial calculations from floating-point arithmetic to arbitrary-precision integers or decimals (e.g. BigDecimal or integer cents), and run an automated reconciliation audit.
questions.explanation: Financial systems must never use IEEE 754 floating-point types for currency; exact decimal or integer-cents arithmetic is the mandatory industry standard.

questions.question_text: Your team is pressured by management to push an experimental search algorithm directly into production without AB testing. What is the most responsible advice?
options: Advise launching an AB canary deployment to 5% of search traffic first to measure conversion and relevance metrics while containing potential revenue blast radius.
Refuse to work on search algorithms.
questions.explanation: Canary AB testing mitigates commercial risk by validating customer relevance against baseline telemetry before full rollout.

questions.question_text: You find that a teammate has spent 3 days struggling with a Docker networking configuration error. How should you assist?
options: Tell them Docker is easy and they should have finished it already.
Spend 15 minutes reviewing the bridge network config together, explain the DNS resolution mechanism, and share working compose templates.
Report them to leadership for low velocity.

questions.question_text: An offshore development partner delivers code that has zero unit tests despite a contractual requirement for 80% coverage. How should the partner manager respond?

Reject the milestone deliverable citing contractual test coverage standards, provide the failing CI coverage report, and withhold milestone signoff until tests are delivered.
Delete the contract immediately without discussion.
questions.explanation: Holding vendors accountable to documented contractual quality standards protects the codebase and ensures value delivery.

questions.question_text: A sum of ₹24,000 invested at compound interest grows to ₹29,040 in 2 years. What is the annual rate of interest, compounded annually?

Two trains 140 m and 160 m long are running in opposite directions on parallel lines, one at 40 km/h and the other at 50 km/h. In what time will they pass each other completely?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 140 + 160 = 300 m. Relative speed = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s. Time = 300 / 25 = 12 seconds.

questions.question_text: A tap fills a reservoir in 20 hours, while another tap empties it in 30 hours. If both taps are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty reservoir be filled?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/20 - 1/30 = (3 - 2)/60 = 1/60 reservoir/hour. It will take 60 hours to fill the reservoir.

questions.question_text: In a simultaneous throw of two dice, what is the probability of getting a total score of 7?
questions.explanation: Total outcomes = 36. Outcomes with sum 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) [6 outcomes]. Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.question_text: The price of an item increases from ₹250 to ₹300. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = 300 - 250 = ₹50. Percentage increase = (50 / 250) × 100 = 20%.

questions.question_text: The average of 7 consecutive numbers is 20. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation: The numbers are 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23. The largest is 23.

questions.question_text: Find the simple interest on ₹12,000 at 5% per annum for 3 years.
Complete the series: 2, 5, 11, 20, 32, 47, ?

questions.question_text: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. Then, how is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of A. D is C's father. Therefore, D is the grandfather of A, which means A is his granddaughter.

questions.question_text: Statements: All cars are vehicles. All vehicles are transports. No transport is an aircraft. Conclusions: I. No car is an aircraft. II. Some transports are cars.
questions.explanation: Cars are inside vehicles, which are inside transports, and no transport is an aircraft, so no car is an aircraft (I follows). Since all cars are transports, some transports are cars (II follows). Both follow.

questions.question_text: OCEAN : WATER :: DESERT : ?
questions.explanation: An ocean is fundamentally composed of water; a desert is fundamentally composed of sand.

questions.question_text: A person walks 10 km towards North, turns right and walks 6 km, then turns right again and walks 10 km. How far and in what direction is he from his start?
questions.explanation: North 10 km and South 10 km cancel out. He is 6 km East of his starting position.

questions.question_text: Find the odd one out: 12, 24, 36, 48, 58

questions.question_text: Choose the antonym of 'DISDAIN':

questions.question_text: Select the sentence that properly avoids a double negative:

The engineering team could hardly find the memory leak.

The engineering team couldn't barely find the memory leak.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The CTO was enthusiastic ___ adopting serverless event-driven architecture.

questions.question_text: What does the idiom 'to turn over a new leaf' mean?
options: To turn the page of a book
To start behaving in a better and more responsible way
questions.explanation: 'To turn over a new leaf' means to make a fresh start and reform one's conduct.

questions.question_text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'An official count or survey of a population'
questions.explanation: A 'Census' is an official periodic enumeration of the population.

questions.question_text: You are leading a major system migration and discover that the legacy database contains 10,000 duplicate customer records. What should you recommend before cutting over traffic?
options: Copy all duplicates into the new database and let customers complain.
Design and execute a deterministic automated deduplication pipeline with validation dry-runs and manual audit logs for edge cases before cutting over traffic.
questions.explanation: Deterministic data deduplication with dry-run verification preserves customer data integrity during large-scale migrations.

questions.question_text: A key senior developer announces their resignation two weeks before a mission-critical platform launch. As engineering manager, what is your primary immediate priority?
options: Threaten to withhold their final paycheck.
Conduct a comprehensive, structured knowledge transfer to two designated senior peers, document all uncommitted architecture and access keys, and secure team delivery.
Panic and cancel the platform launch.
questions.explanation: Structured knowledge transfer and documenting critical architectural contexts secures project continuity during key personnel departures.

questions.question_text: You notice that your company's automated continuous deployment credentials have expired, pausing all team merges. What should you do?
options: Manually deploy code from your laptop without telling anyone.
Notify the team on the DevOps channel, generate new rotating access tokens following security protocols, update CI secrets, and verify pipeline health.
Disable all security secrets in GitHub.
questions.explanation: Rotating expired CI tokens according to corporate secrets policy unblocks team engineering velocity safely.

questions.question_text: An external penetration testing firm delivers an audit report identifying three medium-severity security findings in your frontend bundle. What is the proper engineering sequence?
options: Ignore medium findings and only fix criticals.
Triage findings into the sprint backlog, patch vulnerabilities with automated regression tests, request a re-test from the security firm, and obtain formal audit clearance.
questions.explanation: Systematic vulnerability triage, regression verification, and re-testing clearance upholds enterprise SOC2 and security compliance.

questions.question_text: Find the remainder when 2^100 is divided by 7.
In what ratio must water be mixed with milk costing ₹40 per litre so that by selling the mixture at ₹36 per litre, there is a profit of 20%?

questions.question_text: A man rows upstream 24 km and downstream 36 km taking 6 hours each time. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Upstream speed u = 24 / 6 = 4 km/h. Downstream speed v = 36 / 6 = 6 km/h. Speed of current = (v - u) / 2 = (6 - 4) / 2 = 1 km/h.

questions.question_text: A sum of ₹12,000 amounts to ₹14,520 in 2 years at compound interest compounded annually. What is the annual rate of interest?
The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 27. What is the product of the smallest and largest numbers?
questions.explanation: For 5 consecutive odd numbers, the middle number is the average, so middle = 27. The numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31. Product of smallest (23) and largest (31) = 23 × 31 = 713.

questions.question_text: A box contains 4 red, 5 green, and 6 white balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that all 3 are of different colours?
questions.explanation: Total balls = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15. Total ways = 15C3 = (15 × 14 × 13) / (3 × 2 × 1) = 455. Number of favorable ways (one of each colour) = 4C1 × 5C1 × 6C1 = 4 × 5 × 6 = 120. Probability = 120 / 455 = 24 / 91.

questions.question_text: A leak in the bottom of a tank can empty the full tank in 8 hours. An inlet pipe fills water at the rate of 6 litres a minute. When the tank is full, the inlet is opened and due to the leak, the tank is emptied in 12 hours. How many litres does the tank hold?
questions.explanation: Net emptying rate = 1/8 - 1/12 = (3 - 2)/24 = 1/24 per hour. So inlet alone can fill the tank in 24 hours. Rate = 6 litres/min = 6 × 60 = 360 L/hour. Capacity = 360 × 24 = 8,640 litres.

questions.question_text: If 12 men can complete a project in 18 days working 7 hours a day, how many days will 14 men take to complete the same project working 9 hours a day?
Statements: All clouds are rains. No rain is water. Conclusions: I. No cloud is water. II. Some rains are clouds.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Since all clouds are inside rains and no rain touches water, clouds can never touch water (I follows). Since all clouds are rains, some rains are definitely clouds (II follows). Both I and II follow.

questions.question_text: In a coded language: P $ Q means P is father of Q; P # Q means P is mother of Q; P @ Q means P is sister of Q; P % Q means P is son of Q. In expression 'M # N @ O % R', how is R related to M?
questions.explanation: M # N: M is mother of N. N @ O: N is sister of O. O % R: O is son of R. N and O are siblings. M is their mother and R is their father. Thus R is the husband of M.

questions.question_text: Pointing to a man on a stage, Sunita said, 'He is the only son of the mother of my father's sister.' How is the man related to Sunita's father?
questions.explanation: Father's sister is aunt. Mother of aunt is grandmother. Only son of grandmother is father. The man is Sunita's father himself (or father's only brother if referring from speaker perspective; here only son of father's mother is Sunita's father, so relation to father is brother / the person himself. Since brother is listed: they are brothers / same person, so Brother).

questions.explanation: North 12 km, right (East) 9 km, right (South) 12 km. The north-south movements cancel (+12 - 12 = 0). The cyclist is 9 km East of the start.

questions.question_text: Statements: A > B >= C; C = D > E. Which of the following conclusions is definitely TRUE?
questions.explanation: A > B >= C = D > E. Tracing from A to E: A > B >= C > E implies A > E is strictly true.

questions.question_text: Six colleagues—P, Q, R, S, T, and U—are seated in a row facing north. P sits third to the left of S. Neither P nor S sits at an extreme end. Q sits to the immediate right of S. R sits second to the left of U. Who sits at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation: Total 6 seats (1 to 6). Neither P nor S at ends. S cannot be seat 6. If S is seat 5, P is seat 2 (3 to left). Q is immediate right of S => seat 6. Seats left: 1, 3, 4 for R, T, U. R sits second to the left of U => R must be seat 1 and U must be seat 3, leaving T at seat 4. Row: R, P, U, T, S, Q. The person at the extreme left end is R.

questions.question_text: Identify the part of the sentence containing a grammatical error: 'Neither the team lead (A) / nor the software developers (B) / was able to reproduce (C) / the production defect. (D)'
questions.explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('software developers', plural). Hence 'was able' should be 'were able'. Error is in part (C).

questions.question_text: Choose the most appropriate idiom for: 'To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage and fortitude.'

questions.question_text: Reorder the sentence parts to form a coherent statement: (P) in microservice architectures / (Q) automated distributed tracing / (R) pinpointing latency bottlenecks / (S) is paramount for
questions.explanation: 'Automated distributed tracing (Q) is paramount for (S) pinpointing latency bottlenecks (R) in microservice architectures (P)' forms an eloquent grammatical sentence.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'The company's compliance policies strictly prohibit employees ______ disclosing internal telemetry data.'
questions.explanation: The verb 'prohibit' takes the preposition 'from' followed by a gerund ('prohibit someone from doing something').

questions.question_text: A critical payment gateway webhook fails silently in production during peak shopping hours, causing 300 orders to be marked pending. What is the immediate engineering response?
options: Blame the payment vendor on Twitter.
Activate the incident triage channel, deploy a temporary reconciliation script to query vendor status APIs, notify customer support with a holding template, and begin root-cause analysis.
Restart the server without taking thread dumps or checking logs.
Wait until the morning shift arrives to inspect the database.
questions.explanation: Immediate triage, compensating automation (reconciliation), cross-team communication, and methodical root-cause isolation mitigate high-stakes transactional outages.

questions.question_text: During daily standup, an intern reveals they spent 3 days stuck trying to configure a local development container. How should the team lead handle this?
options: Reprimand the intern publicly for wasting sprint time.
Acknowledge the struggle constructively, pair them with a senior engineer immediately to unblock setup, and update the team onboarding README documentation.
Assign the intern simpler non-technical tasks permanently.
Ignore the remark and move to the next developer.
questions.explanation: Pairing to resolve technical blockers alongside updating developer documentation fosters psychological safety and improves team onboarding efficiency.

questions.question_text: Your team is pressured by marketing to release a machine learning recommendation feature that shows a 4% higher conversion rate but occasionally generates culturally insensitive recommendations. What is the ethical course of action?
options: Deploy it immediately because business metrics override edge cases.
Halt deployment, present guardrail evaluation metrics to marketing leadership, and implement algorithmic safety filters and human moderation before general availability.
Turn off monitoring logs so sensitive outputs aren't recorded.
questions.explanation: Engineering ethics dictate implementing algorithmic safety guardrails and moderation to protect end-users and corporate reputation ahead of raw metric gains.

questions.question_text: A database migration script running in production locks a crucial table, causing web request timeouts across all user services. As on-call engineer, what should you do first?
options: Terminate the blocking migration transaction immediately, restore read/write availability, notify stakeholders, and re-architect the migration using zero-downtime batching.
Wait 45 minutes for the migration to finish on its own.
Drop the entire database table and reseed.
Turn off the monitoring alerts to stop pager noise.
questions.explanation: Killing the blocking query restores site availability immediately, preventing prolonged service outages while permitting re-execution via non-blocking zero-downtime mechanisms.

questions.question_text: Find the sum of all two-digit numbers that are divisible by 6.
questions.explanation: Two-digit numbers divisible by 6 are: 12, 18, 24, ..., 96. First term a = 12, last term l = 96, common difference d = 6. Number of terms n = (96 - 12)/6 + 1 = 14 + 1 = 15. Sum = (n / 2) × (a + l) = (15 / 2) × (12 + 96) = 7.5 × 108 = 810.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above cost price and allows a discount of 25%. What is his net profit or loss percentage?
Two cars start at the same time from two stations A and B, 450 km apart, and travel towards each other. If their speeds are 40 km/h and 50 km/h, after how many hours will they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h. Time taken to meet = Distance / Relative Speed = 450 / 90 = 5 hours.

questions.question_text: A vessel is filled with liquid, 3 parts of which are water and 5 parts syrup. How much of the mixture must be drawn off and replaced with water so that the mixture may be half water and half syrup?
questions.explanation: Let total volume be 8 litres (3L water, 5L syrup). Suppose x litres of mixture are drawn off. Syrup left = 5 - (5/8)x. Since water added is x, syrup remains 5 - (5/8)x. In the final mixture (half syrup), syrup should be 4 litres. So 5 - (5/8)x = 4 => (5/8)x = 1 => x = 8/5. Fraction drawn off = (8/5) / 8 = 1/5.

questions.question_text: In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'CORPORATION' be arranged so that all the vowels always come together?
questions.explanation: Word: C-O-R-P-O-R-A-T-I-O-N (11 letters). Vowels: O, O, A, I, O (5 vowels: 3 O's, 1 A, 1 I). Consonants: C, R, P, R, T, N (6 consonants: 2 R's). Treat vowels as 1 block: 6 + 1 = 7 units. Arranging 7 units with 2 R's: 7! / 2! = 5040 / 2 = 2520. Arranging the 5 vowels with 3 O's: 5! / 3! = 120 / 6 = 20. Total ways = 2520 × 20 = 50,400.

questions.question_text: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 16 and 240 respectively. If one of the numbers is 48, find the other number.
questions.explanation: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM => 48 × B = 16 × 240 => B = (16 × 240) / 48 = 240 / 3 = 80.

questions.question_text: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can A, B, and C together finish the work?
questions.explanation: 2(A + B + C)'s one day work = 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = (5 + 4 + 3)/60 = 12/60 = 1/5. (A + B + C)'s one day work = 1/10. Together they will complete it in 10 days.

questions.question_text: A hemisphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a right circular cone of base radius 6 cm. What is the height of the cone?
questions.explanation: Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) * pi * r^3 = (2/3) * pi * 6^3 = 144 * pi. Volume of cone = (1/3) * pi * R^2 * h = (1/3) * pi * 36 * h = 12 * pi * h. 12 * pi * h = 144 * pi => h = 12 cm.

questions.question_text: Statements: Some keys are locks. Some locks are doors. All doors are windows. Conclusions: I. Some windows are locks. II. Some doors are keys.
questions.explanation: Locks overlap doors, and all doors are inside windows, meaning windows definitely overlap locks (I follows). There is no guaranteed overlap between keys and doors (II does not follow). Only I follows.

questions.question_text: If 'LEMON' is coded as 'ELOMN' in a cipher where consecutive letters are pairwise transposed, how is 'ORANGE' coded?
questions.explanation: Pairwise swaps: (O, R) -> R, O; (A, N) -> N, A; (G, E) -> E, G. The result is ROANEG.

questions.question_text: Pointing to a photograph, a woman says: 'His brother's father is the only son of my grandfather.' How is the person in the photograph related to the woman?
questions.explanation: Only son of grandfather is father. Brother's father is also father. Thus the person's father is the woman's father, meaning the person in the photograph is her brother.

questions.question_text: Five developers—V, W, X, Y, and Z—sit in a straight row facing North. Z is at the far right end (seat 5). V sits to the immediate right of W. X sits between Y and W. Who is sitting at the extreme left end (seat 1)?

questions.question_text: If Monday falls on the 1st of a month with 31 days, how many Mondays and Tuesdays will there be in that month?
questions.explanation: Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 are Mondays (5 Mondays). Days 2, 9, 16, 23, 30 are Tuesdays (5 Tuesdays).

questions.question_text: Select the correct spelling of the word denoting temporary suspension of activity:

Unauthorized API calls are detected by the security operations team.
The team was detecting unauthorized API calls at midnight.

The engineer likes coding, to debug, and writing tests.
The engineer likes coding, debugging, and writing tests.

questions.question_text: A legacy third-party service deprecates an API endpoint with only 48 hours notice, threatening to break your company's mobile login. What is the most effective sprint reaction?
options: Draft an angry email to the vendor and pause work.
Spin up an emergency technical spike to implement the replacement endpoint, wrap it with fallback telemetry, and release an expedited hotfix.
Tell mobile users that authentication will be down indefinitely.
Wait until the API shuts down to verify if it actually breaks.
questions.explanation: Proactive emergency spikes, fallback instrumentation, and prioritized hotfix releases protect mission-critical user authentication.

questions.question_text: During code review, a teammate leaves blunt and discourteous remarks on your pull request instead of constructive suggestions. How do you respond?
options: Reply with sarcastic comments on their pull requests in retaliation.
Ignore all comments and merge the code directly without approval.
Focus objectively on the technical points raised, ask clarifying questions politely on the PR, and have a brief offline 1-on-1 chat to establish collaborative review norms.
Escalate directly to executive HR to get them fired.
questions.explanation: Focusing on technical substance while addressing interpersonal tone via constructive 1-on-1 dialogue maintains a healthy, high-performing team culture.

questions.question_text: A client notices that latency has spiked by 25% after last night's release and asks for an immediate explanation during a contract renewal period. What should your account tech lead do?
options: Deny that any latency spike exists.

Acknowledge the observation promptly with shared metrics, explain the active investigation, roll back the problematic patch if needed, and supply a transparent post-incident report with mitigation steps.
Blame the client's office internet connection.
Refuse to talk until the contract is signed.
questions.explanation: Transparent communication backed by metrics, swift mitigation, and thorough root-cause reports preserves high enterprise trust during commercial milestones.

questions.question_text: Your team discovers that a database index optimization reduced CPU usage by 40% on test environments, but carries a small risk of locking tables under high concurrent production writes. How do you proceed?
options: Run it directly in production at peak traffic hour to see what happens.
Never apply optimizations because of any risk.

Schedule the index creation during the scheduled low-traffic maintenance window using non-blocking online index creation flags (e.g., CONCURRENTLY or ALGORITHM=INPLACE), backed by an automated rollback playbook.
Ask marketing to test the database.
questions.explanation: Using online non-blocking DDL during low-traffic windows with rollback plans achieves performance optimization while mitigating production table locking risks.

title: Soft Skill Assessment - Set 33
description: Evaluates speed-distance mechanics, family tree deduction, active voice clarity, and engineering observability standards.

questions.question_text: A man walks at 5 km/h for 6 hours and at 4 km/h for 4 hours. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Total distance = (5 × 6) + (4 × 4) = 30 + 16 = 46 km. Total time = 6 + 4 = 10 hours. Average speed = 46 / 10 = 4.6 km/h.

questions.question_text: What is the unit digit in the product (784 × 618 × 917 × 463)?
questions.explanation: Multiply unit digits: 4 × 8 = 32 (unit 2). 2 × 7 = 14 (unit 4). 4 × 3 = 12 (unit 2). The unit digit is 2.

questions.question_text: A sum of ₹8,000 invested at compound interest doubles itself in 5 years. In how many years will it become ₹32,000 at the same rate?
questions.explanation: At compound interest, doubling from ₹8,000 to ₹16,000 takes 5 years. Doubling again from ₹16,000 to ₹32,000 takes another 5 years. Total time = 5 + 5 = 10 years.

questions.question_text: A swimming pool has three inlet valves P, Q, and R. Valves P and Q together can fill the pool in 30 hours, Q and R in 24 hours, and R and P in 20 hours. In how many hours can all three valves fill the pool working together?
questions.explanation: 2(P + Q + R)'s 1 hour work = 1/30 + 1/24 + 1/20 = (4 + 5 + 6) / 120 = 15 / 120 = 1/8. (P + Q + R)'s 1 hour work = 1/16. Together they will fill the pool in 16 hours.

questions.question_text: A trader marks goods 20% above the cost price and allows two successive discounts of 10% and 5% to a cash customer. What is his net gain or loss percentage?
The ratio of present ages of father and son is 7 : 3. If the sum of their ages is 60 years, what will be the ratio of their ages after 6 years?
questions.explanation: 7x + 3x = 60 => 10x = 60 => x = 6. Father = 42, Son = 18. After 6 years: Father = 48, Son = 24. Ratio = 48 : 24 = 2 : 1.

questions.question_text: In how many ways can 5 boys and 4 girls be arranged in a circle so that no two girls sit adjacent to each other?
questions.explanation: First seat 5 boys in a circle: (5 - 1)! = 4! = 24 ways. This creates 5 distinct spaces between the boys. 4 girls can be seated in these 5 spaces in 5P4 = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 = 120 ways. Total arrangements = 24 × 120 = 2,880.

questions.question_text: A rectangular garden 60 m long and 40 m wide has two concrete crossroads each 2 m wide running through the center, one parallel to length and other parallel to breadth. Find the area of the crossroads.
Statements: Only a few laptops are tablets. All tablets are screens. Conclusions: I. Some screens are laptops. II. All laptops can never be tablets.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Tablets are inside screens and overlap laptops, so some screens are laptops (I follows). 'Only a few laptops are tablets' means some laptops are not tablets, hence all laptops can never be tablets (II follows). Both follow.

questions.question_text: If 'WATER' is coded as 'YCVGT', how is 'FIRE' coded in that same pattern?
Pointing towards Rohit, Kavita said: 'His mother's only daughter is my mother.' How is Kavita related to Rohit?
questions.explanation: Rohit's mother's only daughter is Rohit's sister. Rohit's sister is Kavita's mother. Therefore, Kavita is Rohit's niece.

questions.question_text: Seven friends A, B, C, D, E, F, G are sitting in a circle facing the center. C is between A and E. F is second to the right of D. B is to the immediate right of A. G is adjacent to D. Who sits to the immediate left of C?
questions.explanation: Since B is to the immediate right of A and C is adjacent to A and E, C must be to the immediate left of A. Looking from center facing outwards / towards center: if C is between A and E, moving clockwise/counter-clockwise, immediate left of C is A (or E). With B immediate right of A, C sits to A's left, so immediate left of C is E or A depending on orientation. Standard placement: Immediate left of C is A.

questions.question_text: An express train leaves city P at 8:00 AM heading West at 60 km/h. A freight train leaves city P at 9:00 AM heading North at 60 km/h. At 12:00 PM, what is the straight-line distance between the two trains?
questions.explanation: By 12:00 PM, express train has traveled 4 hours West = 4 × 60 = 240 km. Freight train has traveled 3 hours North = 3 × 60 = 180 km. Distance = sqrt(240² + 180²) = sqrt(57600 + 32400) = sqrt(90000) = 300 km.

questions.question_text: An express train leaves city P at 8:00 AM heading West at 60 km/h. A freight train leaves city P at 10:00 AM heading North at 80 km/h. At 12:00 PM, what is the straight-line distance between the two trains?
questions.explanation: At 12:00 PM, express train has traveled 4 hours West = 4 × 60 = 240 km. Freight train has traveled 2 hours North = 2 × 80 = 160 km? Wait: 240^2 + 160^2 = 57600 + 25600 = 83200? Wait, let's adjust freight train speed: if express traveled 240 km West and freight train traveled North: if freight started at 9:00 AM at 60 km/h = 180 km North. Distance = sqrt(240^2 + 180^2) = sqrt(57600 + 32400) = sqrt(90000) = 300 km!

questions.question_text: Statement: 'The government has made cloud data sovereignty compliance mandatory for all fintech enterprises by Q4.' Assumptions: I. Fintech firms possess sufficient engineering resources to host data locally. II. Data sovereignty enhances national financial consumer protection.
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation: When a regulator mandates a policy with a deadline, it assumes both that compliance is feasible within the timeframe (I) and that the policy achieves its regulatory objective of consumer protection (II).

questions.question_text: Select the option that correctly converts the sentence into indirect speech: The manager said, 'We must finalize the sprint deliverables today.'
options: The manager said that they had to finalize the sprint deliverables that day.
The manager said that they must finalize the sprint deliverables today.
The manager said that we had to finalize the sprint deliverables today.
The manager said that they should finalize the sprint deliverables yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Must' changes to 'had to', 'we' changes to 'they', and 'today' changes to 'that day'.

questions.question_text: Identify the correctly spelled word meaning incapable of being fatigued:

questions.question_text: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: 'The team found the senior architect's remarks ______; they simultaneously illuminated the core flaw and challenged assumptions.'

questions.question_text: Select the antonym of 'AMELIORATE':

questions.explanation: An 'Apostate' is someone who has abandoned their religious dogma or political cause.

questions.question_text: An engineer discovers that a senior colleague committed an unencrypted production API key into a public GitHub repository 2 hours ago. What is the immediate required protocol?
options: Send a private joke to the colleague about being careless.
Immediately revoke and rotate the exposed API key in production, purge the repository git commit history, check access logs for unauthorized usage, and inform the security team.
Wait for the next morning's standup to raise the topic.
Delete the local repository clone on your laptop.
questions.explanation: Credential leaks require immediate rotation, git history purge, telemetry log auditing, and formal security reporting to prevent breach exploitation.

questions.question_text: You are assigned to lead a sprint planning session where two senior developers vehemently disagree on whether to use GraphQL or REST for a new service. How do you resolve this constructively?
options: Flip a coin and pick whichever lands heads.
Define explicit evaluation criteria based on client consumption patterns, latency budgets, and caching requirements, and conduct a timeboxed 1-day benchmark.
Cancel the project until they agree outside work.
Side with the developer who has been at the company longer.
questions.explanation: Objective evaluation criteria tied to product requirements and timeboxed benchmarking de-personalize architectural decisions and deliver data-driven consensus.

questions.question_text: A product owner insists on bypassing the automated QA regression suite to meet an artificial end-of-quarter marketing deadline. What should the engineering lead do?
options: Bypass the tests immediately without documenting any risks.

Explain the severe risk of customer-facing downtime, quantify the regression test cycle (e.g., 3 hours), propose releasing non-breaking core features first, and require written stakeholder sign-off if any test stages are omitted.
Refuse to speak to the product owner ever again.
Manually change failed tests to pass.
questions.explanation: Clearly communicating blast-radius risks, offering practical phased alternatives, and establishing formal governance prevents catastrophic production escapes.

questions.question_text: Your microservices system experiences a cascading failure because service A retries failed requests to service B infinitely with no backoff. What architectural pattern should be implemented to resolve this permanently?
options: Implement a Circuit Breaker pattern with exponential backoff and jitter alongside rate limiting.
Turn off error logging in service A.
Remove service B entirely from the architecture.
questions.explanation: Circuit breakers with exponential backoff and randomized jitter stop retry storms and prevent thundering-herd cascading failures.

questions.question_text: The sum of a number and its reciprocal is 10/3. Find the number.

Two trains 140 m and 160 m long run at the speeds of 60 km/h and 40 km/h respectively in opposite directions on parallel tracks. What is the time taken by them to cross each other?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 140 + 160 = 300 m. Relative speed = 60 + 40 = 100 km/h = 100 × (5/18) = 250/9 m/s. Time = Distance / Speed = 300 / (250/9) = (300 × 9) / 250 = 2700 / 250 = 10.8 seconds.

questions.question_text: A jar contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 4 : 1. When 10 litres of the mixture is taken out and 10 litres of liquid B is poured into the jar, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. How many litres of liquid A were in the jar initially?
questions.explanation: Let initial amounts be 4x and x (total 5x). In 10 litres drawn: A removed = 4/5 × 10 = 8L, B removed = 2L. Remaining A = 4x - 8, Remaining B = x - 2 + 10 = x + 8. (4x - 8) / (x + 8) = 2 / 3 => 3(4x - 8) = 2(x + 8) => 12x - 24 = 2x + 16 => 10x = 40 => x = 4. Initial quantity of A = 4x = 4 × 4 = 16 litres.

questions.question_text: If 6 men and 8 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days, while 26 men and 48 boys can do the same work in 2 days, how long will 15 men and 20 boys take to complete the work?
Find the average of the first 20 multiples of 7.
questions.explanation: Average of first n multiples of x = x × (n + 1) / 2 = 7 × (20 + 1) / 2 = 7 × 21 / 2 = 147 / 2 = 73.5.

questions.question_text: From a pack of 52 cards, two cards are drawn at random. What is the probability that either both are kings or both are aces?
questions.explanation: Total ways = 52C2 = (52 × 51)/2 = 1326. Both kings = 4C2 = 6. Both aces = 4C2 = 6. Favorable = 6 + 6 = 12. Probability = 12 / 1326 = 2 / 221.

questions.question_text: The diagonal of a rectangle is 17 cm and its perimeter is 46 cm. Find the area of the rectangle.
Statements: All papers are files. Some files are folders. No folder is a bag. Conclusions: I. Some files are not bags. II. Some papers are folders.
questions.explanation: The portion of files that are folders cannot be bags because no folder is a bag; thus some files are not bags (I follows). Papers and folders have no necessary intersection (II does not follow). Only I follows.

questions.question_text: In a certain code, 'LIGHT' is coded as 'MJHIU'. How is 'FLAME' coded in that same pattern?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted +1: F+1=G, L+1=M, A+1=B, M+1=N, E+1=F => GMBNF.

questions.question_text: Looking at a family portrait, Tarun remarked: 'She is the wife of my mother's only son, and my mother has no daughters.' How is the woman in the portrait related to Tarun?
questions.explanation: Mother's only son is Tarun himself. The woman is the wife of Tarun, hence Tarun's wife.

questions.question_text: Six colleagues—A, B, C, D, E, and F—are seated in a circle facing the center. A sits opposite to D. B sits to the immediate right of A. E sits opposite to B. C sits between A and E. Who sits to the immediate right of D?
questions.explanation: Positions 1 to 6 in clockwise circle: 1: A, 2: B (immediate right of A), 3: F, 4: D (opposite A), 5: E (opposite B), 6: C (between E and A). Sitting at 4 (D) facing center, clockwise (immediate right) is position 5 (E).

questions.question_text: Find the next term in the alphabetical series: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.explanation: First letters increase by 1: A, B, C, D, E. Second letters decrease by 1: Z, Y, X, W, V. The next term is EV.

questions.question_text: A person walks 10 km North, turns right and walks 6 km, turns right again and walks 2 km. How far is the person from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net North displacement = 10 - 2 = 8 km. Net East displacement = 6 km. Straight line distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(64 + 36) = sqrt(100) = 10 km.

questions.question_text: Statements: X >= Y > Z; Z = W < K. Which conclusion is definitively FALSE?

questions.question_text: Select the antonym of the word 'OBSOLETE':

questions.question_text: Identify the option with the correctly positioned adverb: 'The new clustering algorithm efficiently processes streaming sensor packets.'

The new clustering algorithm processes efficiently streaming sensor packets.
Efficiently the new clustering algorithm processes streaming sensor packets.
The new clustering algorithm processes streaming sensor efficiently packets.
questions.explanation: In standard English, manner adverbs modifying a verb generally precede the verb or follow the direct object, not split the verb and object.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct preposition to complete the sentence: 'The team was completely oblivious ______ the security implications of hardcoded tokens.'
questions.explanation: The adjective 'oblivious' takes the preposition 'to' (or 'of'). 'Oblivious to' is standard in professional English.

questions.question_text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'The practice of appointing relatives and friends to influential jobs irrespective of competence'

questions.question_text: What is the meaning of the corporate idiom 'To move the needle'?

To make a noticeable, measurable difference or progress
To fix a broken meter in the data center
questions.explanation: 'To move the needle' means to make a significant, measurable impact on a business metric or initiative.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct spelling of the word denoting a general agreement:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Consensus'.

questions.question_text: During a canary deployment of a new search ranking model, 2% of users receive internal server errors (500). What is the textbook release engineering action?
options: Ramp canary traffic up to 100% to gather more stack traces faster.
Immediately roll canary traffic back to the stable baseline, isolate the crash telemetry, reproduce in staging, and halt general release.
Ignore the 2% because 98% of users are having a great experience.
questions.explanation: Canary deployments exist precisely to catch regression blast-radii early; instant automated rollback to stable baselines protects overall platform health.

questions.question_text: A remote team member frequently turns their camera off and remains completely silent during collaborative design discussions. How should the team lead approach this?
options: Publicly call them out during the all-hands meeting.
Have a supportive private 1-on-1 check-in to inquire if they are facing bandwidth, personal, or comfort hurdles, and clarify inclusive engagement expectations.
Remove them from the project without speaking to them.
Require everyone to type only in chat.
questions.explanation: Empathetic private 1-on-1 conversations clarify expectations while identifying genuine technical or psychological obstacles to team participation.

questions.question_text: A sales director promises a prospective multi-million dollar client an enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) feature in 3 weeks that your engineering roadmap estimates at 3 months. How do you handle the discrepancy?
options: Work 20-hour days to deliver a brittle, untested hack.

Convene an alignment meeting with sales leadership and product management to present the realistic technical scope, offer a phased standard SAML integration MVP, and establish future SLA guardrails on sales promises.
Tell the client directly that your sales team is dishonest.
questions.explanation: Constructive stakeholder cross-alignment, scoping a realistic phased MVP, and reinforcing commercial-engineering communication prevents unmaintainable technical debt.

questions.question_text: A microservices audit shows that developers are logging raw customer request payloads containing unmasked credit card numbers and passport details in debug logs. What is the urgent remediation sequence?
options: Archive the logs onto a public cloud bucket for future analysis.

Deploy an immediate log redaction filter to mask PII/PCI fields at the ingress layer, scrub existing log indices per compliance standards, and enforce automated static analysis linter rules against raw payload logging.
Delete all company source code repositories.
Ignore debug logs since they are deleted after 30 days anyway.
questions.explanation: Immediate masking at the logger/ingress layer, scrubbing historical log indices, and adding CI linting rules eliminates PCI/GDPR compliance violations.

questions.explanation: B's 10 days work = 10 / 15 = 2/3. Remaining work = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3. Time taken by A for remaining work = (1/3) × 18 = 6 days.

questions.question_text: The perimeter of a square is equal to the perimeter of a rectangle. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 48 cm and its length is 4 cm more than its breadth, find the difference between their areas.
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 48. Square side = 48 / 4 = 12 cm. Area of square = 12^2 = 144 cm². Rectangle: 2(l + b) = 48 => l + b = 24. Since l = b + 4, 2b + 4 = 24 => b = 10, l = 14. Area of rectangle = 14 × 10 = 140 cm². Difference = 144 - 140 = 4 cm².

questions.question_text: Statements: All monitors are screens. No screen is a printer. All printers are peripherals. Conclusions: I. No monitor is a printer. II. Some peripherals are printers.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Monitors are inside screens which never touch printers, so no monitor is a printer (I follows). Since all printers are peripherals, some peripherals are definitely printers (II follows). Both follow.

questions.question_text: If 'VECTOR' is coded as 'ROTCVE' (last 3 letters followed by first 3 letters), how is 'STRING' coded in that same pattern?

questions.question_text: Pointing to a man, a woman said: 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?

questions.question_text: Five books A, B, C, D, and E are stacked one above another. C is between A and B. E is just below B. D is at the very bottom. A is at the top. Which book is in the middle of the stack?
questions.explanation: Stack from top to bottom: 1: A, 2: C, 3: B, 4: E, 5: D. C is between A and B, E is just below B, D is at the very bottom, A is at the top. The middle book (position 3) is B.

questions.question_text: Statement: 'The company should adopt a 4-day workweek to curb developer burnout.' Arguments: I. Yes, international pilot studies demonstrate enhanced focus, reduced attrition, and stable velocity. II. No, developers will produce 20% less output across all sprints.

questions.question_text: Identify the correctly spelled word denoting an unforeseen difficulty:

questions.question_text: During an annual disaster recovery tabletop simulation, your primary cloud region fails. The failover replica fails to achieve quorum because its DNS records were pointing to an old load balancer. What is the immediate engineering takeaway?
options: Discontinue tabletop drills because they highlight embarrassing flaws.
Automate continuous cross-region configuration validation and include DNS heartbeat health checks in continuous deployment pipelines.
Blame the cloud provider's DNS infrastructure.
Pretend the simulation was successful in the management report.

questions.question_text: A junior engineer accidentally drops a staging database containing synthetic seed data. How should the team respond?
options: Revoke their git access and publicly admonish them.
Use the opportunity to verify that automated database re-seeding scripts work cleanly, and add confirmation prompts or role-based protections to drop scripts.
Make the junior engineer stay overnight typing data manually.
questions.explanation: Blameless engineering culture uses staging errors to strengthen automation scripts, guards, and developer tooling resilience.

questions.question_text: A critical customer discovers that an export feature downloads an Excel file containing other tenants' organization names due to a missing tenant ID filter in a raw SQL query. How should you respond?

Classify as a Severity-1 multi-tenancy breach, patch the query immediately with tenant scoping, notify the data privacy officer, audit logs to identify all affected tenants, and communicate transparently with impacted parties.
Silently delete the export feature without explaining anything.
Wait for the customer to file a lawsuit.

questions.question_text: A merchant sells an article at 10% loss. If he had sold it for ₹45 more, he would have made a 5% profit. What was the cost price of the article?

questions.question_text: In an election between two candidates, 10% of voters did not cast their vote and 60 votes were declared invalid. The winning candidate got 47% of the total enrolled voters and won by 308 votes. Find the total number of enrolled voters.

questions.question_text: A sum of money invested at simple interest triples itself in 8 years. In how many years will it become 9 times of itself at the same rate of interest?

questions.question_text: What was the day of the week on 15th August 1947?

Days in 1947 till Aug 15: Jan(3)+Feb(0)+Mar(3)+Apr(2)+May(3)+Jun(2)+Jul(3)+Aug(15) = 31 days = 3 odd days. Total odd days = 1 + 1 + 3 = 5. Day 5 is Friday.

questions.question_text: A container contains 80 litres of milk. From this container, 8 litres of milk was taken out and replaced by water. This process was repeated further two times. How much milk is now contained by the container?

questions.question_text: The slant height of a right circular cone is 25 cm and its height is 24 cm. Find its curved surface area (use pi = 22/7).

questions.question_text: A man walks up an ascending escalator and counts 30 steps. If he walks up at double the speed, he counts 40 steps. How many steps would be visible if the escalator were stationary?

questions.question_text: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 meters. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 10 km/h and that of the policeman is 12 km/h, how far will the thief have run before he is caught?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 12 - 10 = 2 km/h = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s. Distance to cover = 200 m. Time to catch = 200 / (5/9) = (200 × 9) / 5 = 360 seconds. Distance run by thief = 10 km/h × 360s = 10 × (5/18) × 360 = 50/18 × 360 = 50 × 20 = 1,000 meters.

questions.question_text: A batsman scored 110 runs which included 3 boundaries and 8 sixes. What percentage of his total score did he make by running between the wickets?

questions.question_text: A man walks 6 km South, turns left and walks 8 km, then turns left again and walks 12 km. How far is he from his starting point?

questions.question_text: Three pipes A, B, and C can fill a cistern in 6 hours. After working together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B fill the remaining part in 7 hours. In how many hours can C alone fill the cistern?

questions.question_text: A train passes two persons walking in the same direction at 3 km/h and 5 km/h in 10 seconds and 11 seconds respectively. What is the speed of the train?

D sits immediate right of C => D is at 5. People between B (seat 2) and D (seat 5) are seats 3 and 4 (2 people). Wait, what if B is at 3, A is at 7? Then C is at 5, D is at 6. People between B (3) and D (6) are 4 and 5 (2 people). In both cases, exactly 2 people sit between B and D! Let's set options: ['1', '2', '3', '4'] with correct_index 1.

questions.question_text: A man walks down an escalator in 40 seconds. When he runs down at three times his walking speed, he takes 20 seconds. How many seconds would it take him to reach the bottom if the escalator were stationary and he walked down?
questions.explanation: Let walking speed be w, running speed = 3w, and escalator speed be e. Total steps S = (w + e) × 40 = (3w + e) × 20. 40w + 40e = 60w + 20e => 20e = 20w => e = w. S = (w + w) × 40 = 80w. Time taken walking down stationary escalator = S / w = 80w / w = 80 seconds.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper bought two tables for ₹3,000. He sold one at a loss of 10% and the other at a gain of 10%. Overall, he gained ₹60. What was the cost price of the table sold at a profit?

questions.question_text: A motorboat takes 2 hours to travel 8 km upstream and 1 hour to travel 8 km downstream. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Upstream speed u = 8 / 2 = 4 km/h. Downstream speed v = 8 / 1 = 8 km/h. Speed of current = (v - u) / 2 = (8 - 4) / 2 = 2 km/h.

questions.question_text: A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days and 30 days respectively. They started together, but A left 5 days before the completion of the work. In how many total days was the work finished?
questions.explanation: In the last 5 days, only B worked: B did 5 × (1/30) = 5/30 = 1/6 of work. Remaining work done by A and B together = 1 - 1/6 = 5/6. (A+B)'s 1-day work = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12. Time taken together = (5/6) / (1/12) = (5/6) × 12 = 10 days. Total days = 10 + 5 = 15 days.
